title: Solar radiation did not explain, and dew point explained 0.01-0.03 C per decade of, the extra July-August warming at US stream gauges in 2001-2025; the eastern residual of 0.12 C per decade stayed
abstract: Question: an earlier campaign study (sci:f52b7023) found that July-August water temperature at long-record US stream gauges warmed about 0.10 C per decade more than its year-to-year sensitivity to air temperature and discharge predicts. Do solar radiation and humidity explain this residual? Data: the same USGS gauges and nClimGrid air from the prior bundle; CERES SYN1deg surface solar radiation and MERRA-2 dew point from NASA POWER; HadISDH homogenised station dew point; USCRN ground pyranometers. Method: per-gauge regressions with a year term, HUC2-cluster bootstrap, a pre-set plan, a forward test and a long-window check. Results: in 2001-2025 (189 gauges) the residual trend was +0.069 C per decade (0.021 to 0.147). CERES radiation had no trend at the gauges (-0.35 W m-2 per decade) and removed 0.006 C per decade (-0.017 to 0.019). In 1984-2025, radiation also removed nothing. Water warmed with dew point at fixed air and flow (0.06-0.10 C per C). MERRA-2 dew point removed 0.028 C per decade (0.014 to 0.043), but station dew point (HadISDH) removed only 0.006 (-0.004 to 0.018) in 2001-2024, because the MERRA-2 dew-point trend was twice the station trend, mostly because MERRA-2 was about 1 C lower than HadISDH in 2001-2002. From 2003 both sources agreed and removed 0.012-0.019 C per decade. The residual was all east of 100 W (about +0.12 C per decade) and stayed after both predictors; the West was near zero. 7-day maximum water temperature had no residual. USCRN pyranometers fell 10.5 W m-2 per decade against flat CERES, which is probably sensor drift, so ground data could not confirm the radiation trend. Limitations: non-random, mostly regulated gauges; 1 degree radiation and 5 degree station humidity; linear seasonal-mean models; some regional and start-year checks were exploratory. The cause of the eastern residual stays open.
